subject: maths

moments.title: Gauss's Theorema Egregium
moments.body: Gauss proves the Gaussian curvature of a surface depends only on intrinsic measurements, not on how the surface sits in space. He calls it 'remarkable theorem'.
moments.takeaway: Curvature is intrinsic. You can detect it without leaving the surface.

moments.title: Riemann's habilitation
moments.body: Riemann's lecture, attended by an elderly Gauss, defines manifolds in arbitrary dimensions with a metric. He hints at applications in physics. The lecture is later called the most important in the history of geometry.

moments.title: Einstein uses Riemann
moments.body: Einstein, with help from Marcel Grossmann, uses Riemannian geometry for general relativity. The geometry Riemann hinted at becomes the geometry of spacetime.
moments.takeaway: 60 years after Riemann, his geometry describes the universe.

moments.title: Information geometry
moments.body: Statistical manifolds, equipped with the Fisher information metric, form a Riemannian space. Information geometry now informs ML, particularly natural gradient descent.
moments.takeaway: Statistical estimation lives on a Riemannian manifold.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Differential geometry is central to GR, gauge theory, string theory, robotics, ML. Computer graphics use discrete differential geometry.
now.open_questions: Can geometric deep learning unify ML methods on different domains?

reflection: Riemann hinted at physical applications in 1854. Einstein delivered them in 1915. How long must a mathematical idea wait for its physical destiny?
